statement: On a calendar page, the dates of a month are written in rows of 7, one square for each day of the week. Which date is directly above the 26th?

choices.misconception: I took away 10, as if the calendar had rows of 10 like a hundred square.
I took away 8, which moves up one row and also one square to the left.
I moved one square to the left instead of one row up.
I moved down a row instead of up, so I added 7.

hints: How many dates are in each row of the calendar?
Each row holds 7 dates, so moving straight up one row always changes the date by the same amount. Work out that jump and which way it goes.
Going up one row lands on the date that is 7 smaller.

solutions.reliable: Each row has 7 dates, so the square directly above any date holds the date that is 7 smaller: 26 - 7 = 19. Check: the date directly below the 19th is 19 + 7 = 26. The transferable idea: in a grid with rows of n, one step up means take away n and one step left means take away 1.

whyOnTest: Patterns in a grid: seeing that one row up means taking away the row length is the core idea, and the hundred-square habit of using 10 is offered as a trap.
author: Devansh Sanghavi
